identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Kukke Subramanya Temple, on the Kumaradhara River at the foot of Kumara Parvatha in the Western Ghats of Dakshina Kannada district, is dedicated to Subramanya (Kartikeya), worshipped here in association with serpent deities. In local tradition the serpent king Vasuki is said to have taken refuge here, and the temple is a major centre for serpent-related rites such as Sarpa Samskara and Ashlesha Bali. It is administered by the Karnataka government's Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments (Muzrai) Department.

narrative.summaryIntro:
Kukke Subramanya Temple stands on the banks of the Kumaradhara River in Subramanya village, Kadaba taluk, Dakshina Kannada district, at the foot of Kumara Parvatha in the Western Ghats. It is dedicated to Subramanya (Kartikeya), worshipped here as lord of serpents, and is one of the best-known centres in India for serpent-related rites, particularly Sarpa Samskara and Ashlesha Bali, performed by priests of the Shivalli Madhwa Brahmin community following the ritual manual Tantra Sara Sangraha attributed to Madhvacharya.

The temple is administered by the Karnataka government's Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments (Muzrai) Department, and rituals can be booked through the department's online ITMS portal.
narrative.documentedHistory:
Temple tradition holds that the serpent king Vasuki and other snakes took refuge in caves here while fleeing Garuda, and that Kumaraswamy (Subramanya) and Ganesha defeated the demons Tarakasura and Shurapadma at nearby Kumara Parvatha, after which Kumaraswamy married Devasena; these accounts are recorded in the sources consulted as legend and temple tradition, not as documented history. Karnataka Tourism separately describes the temple as roughly 5,000 years old and among seven sites traditionally associated with the sage Parashurama, a dating that is likewise devotional rather than independently corroborated.

According to Wikipedia, the temple's priesthood changed hands in the early 20th century: the original Sthanika Brahmin priests are stated to have lost their position following involvement in independence activism and consequent pressure under British rule, after which Shivalli Madhwa Brahmins took over performance of rituals under the Tantra Sara Sangraha. Administration passed from the hereditary Koojugodu Kattemane family to the present Muzrai (Hindu Religious Endowments) Department of the Karnataka government.
